reasoning: The claim that generative AI "will replace 300 million jobs" is a misleading overstatement of the primary source from which it derives. The figure originates from a March 2023 Goldman Sachs report (by Jan Hatzius et al.), which estimated that generative AI could "expose" equivalent to roughly 300 million full-time jobs globally to automation. Crucially, the report distinguishes between being "exposed to" automation, being "complemented by" AI, and being "substituted" (replaced) by it. The economists noted that about two-thirds of current jobs are exposed to some degree of AI automation, but most of these would be complemented rather than fully replaced. Additionally, labor economics literature (including analyses by MIT and the Brookings Institution) highlights that technological shifts historically create new occupations and industries, meaning net job losses are not equivalent to the number of jobs exposed to automation.
title: Generative AI will replace 300 million jobs
